markdown_report:
The best early-stage direction is a **bounded, recent-source transition residual**, preserving SASRec when evidence is sparse. Its benefits remain hypotheses until measured on the pinned validation benchmark.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights motivate evidence control: (1) Directed successor relationships can distinguish specific continuations from broad similarity. Separate source/target embeddings express this asymmetry. (2) Distinct-user support can reduce reliance on isolated transitions. Counts measure repeated observations, not functional compatibility. (3) Recent sources can reduce the influence of older interests. A bounded residual limits disruption to SASRec’s generalization.

Three literature insights suggest complementary directions: (1) [ICSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318) supports learning intent structure from histories. Its subsequence alignment does not establish actual purchase purposes. (2) [Directed graph projections](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) motivate asymmetric relationship modeling. Observed transitions still cannot certify complementarity. (3) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates testing negative-sampling objectives. Electronics’ 13.08% training wrong-ranking rate makes separation worth investigating, without establishing validation gains.

**Framework.** Organize methods along three axes: context selection (full history versus recent suffix), relationship evidence (latent similarity versus supported directed transitions), and supervision (single versus multiple negatives). SASRec supplies full-history generalization; the proposed residual adds recent, supported relationships; objective changes provide an independent control.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are 0–10; difficulty increases with score. Each cell gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Recent, support-gated directed residual | 5: specific combination / established components | 7: extensible evidence control / sparse coverage | 8: specific recent continuations / no compatibility guarantee | 7: candidate-specific separation / gains uncertain | 4: small branch / sparse lookup integration |
| B: Uniform multi-negative gBCE | 3: established objective / little novelty | 7: reusable baseline / compute cost | 4: sharper ranking / no explicit current-intent mechanism | 8: targets weak margins / training metrics insufficient | 3: local loss change / calibration care |
| C: Scratch-trained title successor scorer | 5: directional text sharing / familiar approach | 6: supports sparse edges / weak text coverage | 6: finer associations / similarity can mislead | 5: shares evidence / may add noise | 6: available inputs / vocabulary and encoder work |

**Select A at 10% progress.** It explicitly targets two observed user failures: broad associations without specific continuation evidence, and older interests dominating current direction. It targets the model’s weak positive–negative separation through candidate-specific scores. It does not claim to identify satisfied needs.

For recent sources, sum decayed, bounded asymmetric scores weighted by distinct-user source and edge support; cap the total correction. Initialize its amplitude near zero and train jointly. Compare SASRec, A, and objective-only B under matched budgets; select exclusively by four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve routing, splits, seeds, and the predictor writer. Report support coverage and backbone/residual margins; embedding alignment alone is not evidence of collapse.

idea.description: Add a bounded directed transition residual computed from the latest three nonpadding items to each dataset-specific SASRec scorer. Candidate-specific distinct-user transition support gates separate source and target embeddings. Preserve the backbone score wherever transition evidence is absent.
idea.motivation: Recent supported transitions offer an observable proxy for specific continuation relevance, addressing broad association and stale-interest failures. Candidate-specific corrections may improve Electronics’ weak training separation, but neither compatibility nor validation improvement is established by the supplied evidence.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only training histories to build adjacent directed-edge counts, counting each user once per edge and source. At training positions subtract the current user's contribution to both counts, preventing singleton edges from supporting themselves; inference uses complete training counts. Never include validation or test transitions. Use r(h,j)=A*sum_s w_s*g_source(s)*g_edge(s,j)*tanh(dot(U[s],V[j])/sqrt(d)), where suffix weights are nonnegative and sum to one, g_source=n_s/(n_s+tau_s), g_edge=n_sj/(n_sj+tau_e), and A=A_max*sigmoid(a). Start a negative so A is small; use fixed positive shrinkage constants initially. The correction is bounded by A_max. Start with the baseline loss to isolate architecture effects. Do not hard-code stronger Electronics corrections from training diagnostics. Save embeddings, gate parameters, support tables, and hyperparameters beneath the trial directory, and update the predictor writer to implement identical scoring and four-category routing. Retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return metrics and metric_definitions using the actual model and augmented scorer. Preserve the compatibility methods; log2feats may expose backbone states, while predict_score must recover the corresponding causal suffix through an explicit adapter context. Diagnose backbone and augmented margins, support coverage, and residual magnitude without backward passes. Keep metadata categories empty and reviews unavailable. No training or validation results are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
    build distinct-user source/edge counts from training histories
    initialize SASRec and small directed embeddings U,V
    for each causal training position:
        sources = latest_three_nonpadding_items(prefix)
        counts = training_counts minus current_user_contributions
        base_pos, base_neg = SASRec scores
        residual(candidate) = bounded_supported_transition_score(sources, candidate, counts)
        optimize baseline_loss(base_pos + residual(pos), base_neg + residual(neg))
    save model, counts, and scorer configuration
    write predictor with the same scoring rule and category routing
Compare controlled variants using pinned macro validation HR@10 only.

originality.positive: Combines candidate-specific distinct-user support, recent causal sources, and a bounded asymmetric residual.
originality.negative: Directed embeddings, shrinkage, recency weighting, and residual gates are established components.

future_potential.positive: Provides an interpretable foundation for studying when collaborative transition evidence should influence sequential recommendations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse supported edges may sharply limit coverage, and transitions need not express useful complementarity.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains SASRec and adds a small scoring branch with sparse count lookups.
code_difficulty.negative: Leave-user-out support, aligned causal scoring, checkpoint serialization, and diagnosis/predictor parity require careful integration.

related_work.title: ICSRec
contributions: Learns intent representations through subsequence alignment and clustered intent prototypes.
limitations: Does not establish actual purchase purpose, satisfaction, or gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph Projections
contributions: Uses directed weighted projections of user–item interactions to infer complementary relationships.
limitations: Does not establish that every sequential transition represents functional compatibility or validate the proposed support gate.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Reducing Overconfidence in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates calibrated binary cross-entropy and increased negative sampling as controlled SASRec improvements.
limitations: Objective improvements require benchmark-specific validation and do not explicitly resolve current-intent or satisfied-need errors.
